title: Amend the Tip on fix/agentic-default
description:
**SITUATION:**

This lab picks up where lab 2 left off. Open `~/sprint-service` and you should already be on `fix/agentic-default`. That branch has **three** commits ahead of `main` (config → `beta`, README run notes, version banner), and those commits are **already on `origin`** — same as after you ran `git push -u origin fix/agentic-default` in lab 2. Local `main` still has the bug: `agentic_sprints_default = full`. Do not touch `main`.

In standup, someone asked for the short write-up that belongs with that default flip — why Core keeps the global default on beta, and why the rescue stayed on a fix branch instead of landing on `main`. You agreed, then pushed the branch without the file. It is sitting in your working tree untracked: `docs/agentic-default.md`. `git status` will show it; `git show --stat HEAD` will show a tip that does not include it yet.

If you make a **fourth** commit (“add forgotten writeup”), the branch history stops looking like three clean stories and starts looking like a cleanup afterthought. Instead, **amend the tip**: fold `docs/agentic-default.md` into the last of those three commits so the log still has exactly three entries, and the tip finally matches what you meant to ship.

Amending only rewrites your **local** tip. Because that tip was already published, `origin/fix/agentic-default` still points at the old commit until you update it. A plain first-style push will not fast-forward after a rewrite — you must get the new tip onto the remote so `origin/fix/agentic-default` matches your new HEAD. Leave `main` alone on both sides.

Your identity (`Ada Learner`) is already configured. `origin` is `git.forgeboard.internal`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Confirm you are on `fix/agentic-default`, that you have exactly three commits ahead of `main`, and that `docs/agentic-default.md` is still untracked.
2. Stage only the writeup `docs/agentic-default.md`.
3. Fold the writeup into the **existing tip** on this branch — do not add a fourth commit. Keep one clear subject in the same theme (not a “forgot the doc” follow-up).
4. Confirm you still have exactly three commits and a clean working tree, then **push the rewritten tip to `origin`** so `origin/fix/agentic-default` matches your new HEAD (a plain push will not fast-forward after a tip rewrite).
5. Leave local and remote `main` exactly as they are.

problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Amend the Tip on fix/agentic-default

## 1. Inspect

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
git branch --show-current     # fix/agentic-default
git status                    # docs/agentic-default.md untracked
git log --oneline main..HEAD  # three commits, already on origin
git show --stat HEAD
```

## 2. Fold the writeup into the tip

```bash
git add docs/agentic-default.md
git commit --amend --no-edit
git log --oneline main..HEAD  # still three commits, new tip SHA
```

## 3. Publish the rewritten tip

Plain `git push` is rejected — the old tip is already on origin. Update **your** fix branch:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin fix/agentic-default
git status
git log --oneline --all --graph
```

Leave `main` alone.

## Rule of thumb

Amend rewrites the tip. After that tip was already pushed on an unmerged fix branch, update origin with `--force-with-lease`. Never plain `--force`, and never rewrite `main`.
